roles.responsibility: Record source lineage, citations, rights claims, and provenance concerns without treating declarations as authentication.
Review TEI witnesses, collation output, variant readings, and textual or authority assertions.
Maintain passage-to-adaptation mapping, genre boundaries, and speculative disclosures.
Own scene and shot manifests, keyframe references, and render instructions.
Coordinate render task and take records, provider declarations, and contributor submissions.
Review declared technical evidence, findings, motion checks, defects, and accessibility concerns.
Apply the declared vote policy, record selection outcomes, and triage vote appeals.
Maintain the ordered timeline, continuity notes, frame-chain evidence, and assembled-media references.
Review supplied translations, subtitle cues, language metadata, and declared audio-track artifacts.
Collect release-candidate gate evidence, hazard screening, credits, and verification limitations.
Approve the versioned release record and preserve links to superseded releases and corrections.
Triage post-release issues, identify artifact owners, request missing evidence, and coordinate corrective PRs.

gates.title: Project intake exists
criteria: A scoped intake request is recorded in a tracked project artifact.

gates.title: Scope and accountable contact are recorded
criteria: Project scope and a role-based contact route are recorded.
Declared contributor identity is not treated as verified identity.

gates.title: Source lineage record is structurally reviewed
criteria: Source identifiers, citations, rights notes, and lineage links are recorded where known.
Unverified source claims and unresolved rights questions are disclosed.

gates.title: Source concern is reported for intake review
criteria: The concern identifies the affected source, witness, or passage and includes evidence.
The source steward reviews the declared lineage before any artifact is changed.

gates.title: Downstream source concern is sent back to intake
criteria: A release review identifies a source-lineage concern and links the affected artifact.
The concern returns to source_intake for human review.

gates.title: Post-release owner is confirmed
criteria: A human triager identifies the affected artifact type and checks artifact_owners.
Unknown or cross-stage ownership stays in triage until a human assigns it.
A destination stage receives a correction request, not an automatic content change.

gates.title: Rejected attestation is returned to textual review
criteria: The rejected attestation reference and the associated witness or assertion are identified.
The textual editor reviews the affected declaration; rejection is not represented as a cryptographic verification result.

gates.title: Release review flags an attestation
criteria: A rejected or unavailable attestation is linked to the affected textual record.
The issue returns to textual_collation for a human source and witness review.

gates.title: TEI collation output is reviewed
criteria: TEI apparatus entries are parsed as data and readings are grouped by witness.
A human records interpretation, uncertainty, and any selected reading.

gates.title: Adaptation brief is approved
criteria: The brief links to reviewed passages and records its declared genre.
Canonical and speculative material remain clearly distinguished by human review.

gates.title: Canonical mismatch returns to adaptation
criteria: Evidence identifies the affected adaptation and the relevant source or passage.
The adaptation lead reviews the mapping before making a corrective change.

gates.title: Shot manifest meets structural constraints
criteria: Duration, keyframe anchors, genre, and required action fields pass structural validation.
A human reviews narrative meaning and continuity before render handoff.

gates.title: A render take is recorded
criteria: A take record identifies its task, provider declaration, artifact, and digest.
The record does not imply that this repository rendered or remotely verified the media.

gates.title: Render failure is classified for redesign
criteria: Failure evidence distinguishes a retry from a change to shot instructions or keyframes.
Any design change returns to shot_design through a reviewed artifact change.

gates.title: Storyboard defect is reported during rendering
criteria: A render-stage report identifies a shot or storyboard artifact and supporting evidence.
The shot designer confirms any requested design change.

gates.title: Technical review findings are recorded
criteria: Review findings identify the subject, method, status, assessor, and available evidence.
Declared motion checks are not represented as video decoding or a media-quality proof.

gates.title: Failed take is returned for a controlled retry
criteria: A reviewer links the failed take and explains whether a retry is appropriate.
A new take is a new artifact and must be reviewed independently.

gates.title: Liveness concern is reviewed before rerender
criteria: The finding identifies the take, method, and supporting evidence.
A human decides whether the result warrants a rerender or an inconclusive finding.

gates.title: Anachronism concern is returned for adaptation review
criteria: The report cites the scene or shot and explains the apparent mismatch.
A human adaptation reviewer checks the declared genre and disclosure.

gates.title: Technical review confirms a storyboard defect
criteria: Finding references the affected shot or keyframe and records the observed defect.
The shot designer reviews the evidence before updating the manifest.

gates.title: Declared quorum and selection policy are met
criteria: The local tally meets the configured distinct-voter quorum and produces a deterministic result.
Identity and reputation evidence remain declarations unless separately verified.

gates.title: Vote appeal is returned for human reconsideration
criteria: Appeal identifies the vote policy, affected result, and evidence.
A moderator records an appeal disposition before any result is changed.

gates.title: Downstream vote appeal returns to selection
criteria: Release review identifies an appeal tied to a selection result and records its evidence.
The community moderator reviews the original policy and tally.

gates.title: Timeline metadata is internally consistent
criteria: Shot durations and declared timeline order are reviewed for gaps and continuity.
A frame chain covers supplied digests and timestamps only; it does not imply media muxing.

gates.title: Release review detects a continuity concern
criteria: The concern identifies a timeline, clip, shot, or continuity note and includes evidence.
Assembly reviews the timeline correction before it is accepted.

gates.title: Supplied localization artifacts pass available checks
criteria: Language metadata and caller-supplied subtitle cue windows are checked.
Translation quality, audio synthesis, and phonetic alignment are not inferred.

gates.title: Translation correction is reported during localization
criteria: The report identifies language, cue or passage, and proposed correction.
A qualified human reviewer approves any translation change.

gates.title: Release review returns a translation correction
criteria: The finding references the affected localization artifact and evidence.
The localization lead reviews the correction and its effect on the release candidate.

gates.title: Subtitle timing issue is reported
criteria: The report identifies the cue, shot window, and observed timing issue.
Corrected cue boundaries are reviewed against the current timeline.

gates.title: Release review returns a subtitle timing issue
criteria: The finding identifies the cue and expected timeline or shot window.
The localization lead reviews the corrected cue before release.

gates.title: Dub audio issue is reported
criteria: The issue identifies the declared audio-track artifact and available timing evidence.
A reviewer records whether the issue is audio quality, timing, or unsupported alignment.

gates.title: Release review returns an audio issue
criteria: The report references the declared audio track and the expected correction.
No generated audio or phonetic alignment is assumed to exist.

gates.title: Release-candidate evidence is reviewed
criteria: Available schema, test, timeline, provenance, and safety evidence is attached.
Manual gates remain explicit; structural validation is not presented as formal proof.

gates.title: Credits and provenance are checked
criteria: Credit entries and contribution references are reviewed for completeness.
A digest check is not treated as authentication of a contributor.

gates.title: Release-stage credits issue is reported
criteria: The release record links the affected credit or provenance artifact.
Assurance reviews the ledger and any correction proposal.

gates.title: Versioned release record is published
criteria: A release manifest identifies the version, artifacts, and release notes.
Previously published artifacts remain identifiable for later corrections.

gates.title: Issue event is available to triage
criteria: A GitHub issue event document is supplied to the local router or a configured Action.
No always-on listener or online webhook receiver is implied.

gates.title: Release defect is routed to triage or a typed owner
criteria: An untyped or cross-stage report stays with the feedback triager.
One recognized typed artifact may route to its declared owner for review.
Routing never edits or releases an artifact automatically.

gates.title: General feedback receives a human disposition
criteria: The report is classified, linked to evidence when available, and assigned for follow-up.
Missing or ambiguous information is requested rather than silently converted into a fix.

gates.title: Feedback disposition is retained
criteria: Issue, owner decision, correction PR, review evidence, and resulting release are cross-linked.
Repository history records the change only after it is pushed and reviewed.

transitions.trigger: Source lineage and passage scope are reviewed.
The collation decision and its limits are recorded.
The adaptation brief and genre disclosure are approved.
The shot manifest and render instructions pass their declared checks.
A render take is submitted for review.
Required technical review findings are recorded as acceptable for selection.
The declared selection policy reaches its required quorum.
The timeline and assembled-media references are reviewed.
Supplied localization artifacts are reviewed and recorded.
Required release-candidate evidence is reviewed by people accountable for the gates.
A published release accepts issue and feedback intake.
A source-provenance concern needs source-level review.
A downstream source-provenance concern is confirmed.
A rejected attestation is linked to a textual witness or assertion.
Release review rejects a declared attestation on a textual record.
A canonical mismatch requires the adaptation-to-source mapping to be reviewed.
Technical review confirms a storyboard defect in a shot or keyframe.
A render failure requires a new or corrected take.
A liveness or motion finding requires a new take or human reassessment.
An anachronism flag requires review of narrative framing and disclosure.
An appeal is received while the selection decision is being reviewed.
Release review identifies a vote appeal that needs moderator review.
A timeline-continuity defect requires the assembly record to be reopened.
A translation correction is reported during localization review.
Release review returns a translation correction for human review.
A subtitle timing issue is reported during localization review.
Release review returns a subtitle timing issue for correction.
A dub-audio issue is reported during localization review.
Release review returns an audio issue for correction.
A credits discrepancy is reported for assurance review.
A published release defect is reported for triage.
A release defect is recorded for triage or typed-owner resolution.
General feedback is recorded for human triage.
A human triager confirms source_intake owns the affected artifact.
A human triager confirms textual_collation owns the affected artifact.
A human triager confirms adaptation owns the affected artifact.
A human triager confirms shot_design owns the affected artifact.
A human triager confirms volunteer_render owns the affected artifact.
A human triager confirms technical_review owns the affected artifact.
A human triager confirms community_selection owns the affected artifact.
A human triager confirms assembly owns the affected artifact.
A human triager confirms localization owns the affected artifact.
A human triager confirms release_assurance owns the affected artifact.
A human triager confirms release owns the affected artifact.

feedback_routes.reason: Recheck the declared source lineage and evidence with the source steward; a declaration is not proof of authenticity.
Return the rejected textual witness or assertion attestation to the textual editor for source-linked review; no cryptographic verification is implied.
Return the cited mismatch to the adaptation lead to review passage mapping and declared genre; revisit collation through a separate reviewed change if needed.
Ask the shot designer to inspect the referenced scene, shot, or keyframe and propose a reviewed change.
Ask the volunteer coordinator to assess the failed task or take and determine whether a retry or design revision is needed.
Return the reported liveness or motion concern for human review and a decision about rerendering; no automatic media inference is implied.
Ask the adaptation lead to review the cited detail against the declared genre and disclosure.
Have the community moderator review the policy, quorum record, and appeal evidence before changing a result.
Return the affected timeline or continuity finding to assembly for a reviewed correction.
Ask the localization lead to review the supplied translation and document the correction and reviewer.
Ask the localization lead to check the cited cue boundaries against the shot and timeline.
Ask the localization lead to review the declared audio track and its alignment evidence; synthesis is not implied.
Have assurance review credit completeness and provenance records, then route any correction to its confirmed artifact owner.

Start with the feedback triager; a single recognized typed artifact reference may route to its declared owner, while unknown or cross-stage reports remain in triage. No automatic artifact change is made.
Record and triage general feedback; a human selects an upstream owner when the affected artifact or route becomes clear.

contribution_routes.reason: Submit a candidate source and citation or rights evidence for source-steward review; the proposal does not authenticate the material.
Propose a transcription artifact linked to its witness and evidence for textual-editor review.
Submit a scholarly review note and supporting references for human evaluation; the route itself makes no authority determination.
Propose a passage-linked adaptation change for genre, disclosure, and source-mapping review.
Propose a scene, shot, or keyframe blueprint for structural and human continuity review.
Offer a render-take artifact for declared task association and human review; the route does not create media.
Submit a review finding with its method and evidence for technical-review triage; submission is not an automated media-quality verdict.
Propose a timeline or assembly artifact change for continuity and evidence review.
Submit caller-supplied localization text or subtitle cues for language and human review; no translation is generated by routing.
Offer a declared voice or audio artifact for consent, licensing, timing, and human review; routing neither synthesizes nor aligns audio.
Propose a contributor credit or provenance correction for assurance and contributor review; the claim is not identity-verified by submission.
Propose a release-package artifact or revision for release-manager review; no publication occurs from an issue or route alone.
